correctness.rationale: For each triple with a pre-update A agents, individual outputs are Binomial(3,a/3) at (c30,c21)=(0,1/3) and Binomial(3,1−a/3) at (1,2/3). Mixed triples have variance 2/3; the expected number under fresh uniform triple partition with k A agents is k(N−k)/(N−1). Consequently conditional K-next mean is k or N−k and conditional variance 2k(N−k)/[3(N−1)]. H(k)=k(N−k) is a one-step eigenfunction with q_N=1−2/[3(N−1)] on both corners. H is bounded above N²/4 and below N−1 off unanimity, hence two-sided geometric survival bounds, finite a.s. hitting, matching log(q_N) exponent; martingale/signed martingale yields initial A-fraction phase probability. Complement kernel duality gives reversal interpretation. Handles N=3, k=0,N boundaries without asserting positive tail there.

value.rationale: Two deterministic neutral singular corners do not describe stochastic finite populations. An exact all-N absorption-rate baseline and alternating consensus selection distinguish independent individual activation from shared group flipping, and quantify the scale of stochastic drift. The model is specified enough to be a meaningful benchmark rather than a generic voter slogan.

final_claim: In the annealed three-agent majority model with independent individual contrarian activations, the neutral and reversal corners have exact N-dependent heterozygosity eigenvalue 1−2/[3(N−1)] for every N divisible by three, almost-sure entry into the unanimous set, sharp geometric survival-tail rate, and initial-share consensus or alternating-phase probabilities.
limitations: Uniform fresh partitions of N divisible by three, independently resampled agent activations, only exact two corners, finite-population tail rate not full finite-time hitting distribution; no claim for permanently assigned contrarian personalities.
residual_risks: General neutral-drift sampling models may encode the exact variance after a nontrivial identification; no full priority certificate.
